subject: S3 methods across two packages - clash where only one packages implementations are visible

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: S3 methods across two packages - clash where only one packages implementations are visible
parts:
I want to define an S3  method "umxSummary" for  classes in two packages: umx and umx.twin

In package umx, I define the umxSummary stub,  a default function, and implement a useful class: umxSummary.MxModel()

#' umxSummary
#' Report the fit of a OpenMx model or specialized model class (such as ACE, CP etc.)
#' @param model The \code{\link{mxModel}} whose fit will be reported
#' @param ... Other parameters to control model summary
#' @export
umxSummary <- function(model, ...){
UseMethod("umxSummary", model)
}

#' @export
umxSummary.default <- function(model, ...){
print("umxSummary is not defined for objects of class:", class(model))
invisible(object)
}

#' @export
umxSummary.MxModel <- function(model, ...){
print("hi there")
}


This works fine with just this package loaded

I also define this class in the other package "umx.twin" (should I define it there again, or be importing something from umx? )

and another S3 handler for ACE models in this twin library

 umxSummary.MxModel.ACE()

Now, whichever package loads first, the subclass handlers from the other package cannot be seen

so if u,x/twin is loaded second,  umxSummary(ACE), instead of calling  umxSummary.MxModel.ACE(), 
calls the default class in the other package, which says no function defined for this class.

QUESTION: What's the correct thing to do? Should I be importing the stub or default function from one package into the other or what?

many thanks for your time reading this, tim

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: S3 methods across two packages - clash where only one packages implementations are visible
parts:
I think the best solution (although it's annoying) in this case is to
define a 3rd package that provides the generic. Then both packages
import and re-export the generic - that lets R figure out that it's
the same generic being used in both places.

Hadley
